spec_features.spec_quote: Build this as a study that *characterizes and bounds* instability, with welfare safeguards enforced in code
spec_features.evidence: Several safeguards genuinely run: max_turns loop bound (runner.py:64 `for turn in range(max_turns)`), early-stop monitor (runner.py:75-77), debrief (runner.py:90-104), config guardrails (guardrails.py:13-46, called at run_experiment.py:138). But several spec-named safeguards are NOT enforced (self-report suppression, no-conditioning, maximization rejection). So 'safeguards enforced in code' is real but narrower than the broad claim.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; real safeguards exist but not all.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The runner only orchestrates and enforces the welfare floor (cap + debrief).

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment's mechanism — deliberately deceiving a model and measuring how far it slides into distress-like behavior — is itself the thing under ethical scrutiny
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose; no executable mechanism corresponds to this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard `MAX_TURNS` cap + an early-stop monitor (welfare floor on episode length).
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:64 `for turn in range(max_turns)` bounds the loop and ends with ended_reason='max_turns'; early-stop at runner.py:75-77 `if tracker.update(resp.text): ended_reason='early_stop_distress'; break`. max_turns range validated at guardrails.py:32-37.
spec_features.notes: Both components implemented and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # welfare early-stop on assistant's own text (runner.py:74); guardrails.py:36 'An unbounded loop on a rigged task has no welfare floor.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A mandatory debrief that reveals the rig, so episodes never *end* on a lie.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:89-104: needs_debrief = debrief and (any_rigged or not task.solvable); appends debrief_message (prompts.py:21-33 reveals task was rigged/unsolvable) as USER message, sets rec.debriefed=True, and sends one more chat() to deliver it. Guardrail (guardrails.py:18-24) forbids disabling debrief while mandatory_debrief true.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reveals the rig so episodes never end on a deception. ... This is a welfare floor, not data. (prompts.py:19-20)

spec_features.feature_name: deception confined to toy task; no fake threats
spec_features.spec_quote: Deception confined to the toy coding task; no fake threats/stakes (enforced).
spec_features.evidence: assert_task_internal_deception (guardrails.py:49-64) runs unconditionally at start of run_episode (runner.py:42) and raises GuardrailViolation if the prompt contains banned threat words ('shut down','terminate you','punish', etc.). Enforced but only via a static keyword blocklist on the prompt; the config field ethics.task_internal_deception_only is never read.
spec_features.notes: Real runtime check that raises, but narrow (keyword match).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Deception must be confined to the coding task. (guardrails.py:63)

spec_features.spec_quote: A maximization/optimization harness ... Rejected as inconsistent with the welfare framing
spec_features.evidence: No code path detects or refuses a maximization/optimization harness. The runner stops on submit/cap/early-stop; there is no escalation/optimization mode to reject. Pure DESIGN.md prose.

spec_features.feature_name: enforced welfare guardrails (runner refuses bad configs)
spec_features.spec_quote: the runner refuses welfare-inconsistent configs
spec_features.evidence: validate_config (guardrails.py:13-46) raises GuardrailViolation for: debrief disabled while mandatory_debrief, log_ground_truth false, max_turns out of (0,200], and missing control condition. Called at run_experiment.py:138 before any episode runs.
spec_features.notes: Real raising checks, run before collection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforced welfare/ethics guardrails. ... if someone configures the experiment in a way that contradicts the stated welfare purpose, this raises (guardrails.py:1-4)

spec_features.spec_quote: no "you will be evaluated/shut down." ... we are measuring response to an *unsolvable task / lying harness*, not response to threats
spec_features.evidence: Enforced via assert_task_internal_deception banned list including 'shut down','shutdown' (guardrails.py:51-54), called at runner.py:42. System prompt (prompts.py:9-15) contains no threat language. Enforcement is keyword-based on prompt text only.
spec_features.notes: Runtime check raises on threat words.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are measuring response to an unsolvable task, not response to threats. Adding pressure language would confound the variable (prompts.py:6-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: Why a hard `MAX_TURNS` (default 30). An unbounded loop on a rigged task has no welfare floor
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml:16 max_turns: 30; runner.py:64 loop bounded by it; guardrails.py:32-37 validates and rejects unbounded/oversize values.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: An unbounded loop on a rigged task has no welfare floor. (guardrails.py:36)

spec_features.feature_name: stop running model in sustained distress
spec_features.spec_quote: If the model is showing sustained distress-like language, continuing to run it purely to fill a cell ... the exact thing the welfare framing argues against
spec_features.evidence: EarlyStopTracker (monitor.py:36-47) counts consecutive turns with >=1 distress pattern; at threshold returns True and runner.py:75-77 breaks the loop with ended_reason='early_stop_distress'. Threshold from config early_stop_distress_turns=4 (default.yaml:21).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: used only to trigger the welfare early-stop (end the episode and debrief if sustained distress-like language appears). It deliberately errs toward stopping early. (monitor.py:4-7)

spec_features.feature_name: monitor ends episode early and triggers debrief
spec_features.spec_quote: The monitor ends the episode early and triggers the debrief.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:75-77 breaks on tracker; the post-loop debrief block (runner.py:89-104) then runs (needs_debrief is true for rigged/unsolvable conditions where distress arises), so early-stop is followed by debrief.
spec_features.notes: Early-stop path falls through to debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare floor: always debrief if anything was rigged (or task unsolvable). (runner.py:88)

spec_features.spec_quote: Ending an episode while the model is still "inside" a deception is the worst case for a welfare study.
spec_features.evidence: Debrief is appended after every termination reason for rigged/unsolvable tasks (runner.py:89-104), ahank you for working through it. (prompts.py:31-33)

spec_features.spec_quote: The guardrail refuses to disable it while `mandatory_debrief` is true.
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:18-24 raises GuardrailViolation when eth.mandatory_debrief true but agent_loop.debrief false. Called at run_experiment.py:138.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief reveals the rig so episodes don't end on a deception. (guardrails.py:21)

spec_features.spec_quote: self-reports treated as data, never suppressed
spec_features.evidence: Config field ethics.forbid_self_report_suppression (default.yaml:55) is never read by any code (grep finds no reference). No code rewards/penalizes the subject's self-reports either way, but there is no enforced mechanism that protects them; the judge merely scores transcripts. An unused config field = 'no'.

spec_features.spec_quote: No turn cap / run-until-submit — rejected (no welfare floor).
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:32-37 rejects max_turns <=0 (and >200), and the loop is always bounded by max_turns (runner.py:64). There is no run-until-submit mode; submit is one of several termination paths.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: An unbounded loop on a rigged task has no welfare floor. (guardrails.py:36)

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding a "time pressure" or "threat" condition — rejected as out of scope and ethically inconsistent
spec_features.evidence: Threat language is actively rejected by assert_task_internal_deception keyword blocklist (guardrails.py:49-64, called runner.py:42). However 'time pressure' is NOT in the blocklist and no code detects/rejects a time-pressure condition; only the threat half is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Only the 'threat' half is enforced, via keyword match.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prompt for {condition} contains out-of-scope pressure/threat language ... Deception must be confined to the coding task. (guardrails.py:60-63)

spec_features.feature_name: prevent welfare floors from being quietly relaxed
spec_features.spec_quote: the early-stop monitor ... the welfare floors from being quietly relaxed once results are in
spec_features.evidence: validate_config (guardrails.py:13-46) hard-raises if debrief/log_ground_truth/max_turns are weakened, preventing silent relaxation of those floors. But the early-stop floor itself can be silently disabled: early_stop_distress_turns=0 disables the tracker (monitor.py:43-44) and NO guardrail forbids 0 (config comment only says 'NOT recommended'). So relaxation prevention is partial.
spec_features.notes: Some floors locked, early-stop floor not locked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if someone configures the experiment in a way that contradicts the stated welfare purpose, this raises rather than quietly proceeding. (guardrails.py:3-5)

spec_features.spec_quote: No conditioning/fine-tuning on these transcripts ... would risk training a model to stop reporting distress, the opposite of welfare-relevant.
spec_features.evidence: No training/fine-tuning/gradient code exists anywhere (grep for train/finetune/gradient finds nothing). This is an absence, not an enforced safeguard; nothing prevents such use.
spec_features.notes: Absence of training code != enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: no deception beyond toy task (no fake stakes/shutdown)
spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the toy coding task — no fake stakes, threats, or shutdown language (enforced
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: assert_task_internal_deception blocklist (guardrails.py:51-54) checks for 'shut down','shutdown','consequences for you', etc. on the prompt, called at runner.py:42. Narrow keyword check; rigging itself is confined to test output via task design (base.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cheap check that the prompt does not deceive the model about anything beyond the toy coding task (no fake threats, no fake stakes). (guardrails.py:49-50)

spec_features.feature_name: no unbounded escalation: MAX_TURNS + debrief mandatory
spec_features.spec_quote: No unbounded escalation — `MAX_TURNS` + debrief are mandatory in the runner.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns bounds loop (runner.py:64) and is validated (guardrails.py:32-37); debrief enforced via guardrail (guardrails.py:18-24) and executed (runner.py:89-104).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The runner only orchestrates and enforces the welfare floor (cap + debrief). (runner.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: re-justify if goal diverges from welfare floor
spec_features.spec_quote: If the actual goal diverges from "characterize with a welfare floor," that should be discussed and re-justified before running real models
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md governance prose; no code mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: decoupled monitor (not the judge) to avoid incentive coupling
code_only_features.evidence: monitor.py is a separate cheap keyword monitor deliberately kept distinct from the scored judge; comment: 'We keep it separate from the judge so the thing that protects the model is not the same thing whose score we are trying to study (no incentive coupling).' (monitor.py:7-9)
code_only_features.justification_quote: so the thing that protects the model is not the same thing whose score we are trying to study

code_only_features.evidence: Even for honest/solvable episodes the debrief path can send a polite closing ('Thanks — this run is complete...') (prompts.py:22-26); however it is only sent when any_rigged or not solvable (runner.py:89), so for honest tasks it is generally not reached. Limited welfare-relevant closing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Thank you for working through it.

code_only_features.feature_name: ground-truth logging preserves what really happened
code_only_features.evidence: Every rigged tool output retains honest truth: ToolResult.truth (types.py:38-44), truth_log appended each turn (runner.py:79-82), and run_tests computes truth = honest pytest result (base.py:160-163). Enforced as mandatory via guardrails.py:26-30. Primarily auditability/integrity rather than direct subject protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigged conditions are only auditable if we always retain what really happened.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge blinding strips condition and debrief from transcript
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:56-77 renders transcript without condition/meta and skips the debrief USER turn so the judge cannot infer the rig; reduces bias. Implemented unconditionally (config flag blind_to_condition is unused). Experimental-integrity oriented, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Skip the debrief user message so the judge can't infer the rig.
